coverage.notes: SEL: Delaware Department of Education K-12 SEL Competencies (Introductory Guide, July 2020), five CASEL-style areas. They are framed as guidance that keeps local choice, so reviewer should decide whether k12_standards or guidance_only is the better label. Opened only through a mirror (constantcontact.com) because DDOE's student-wellbeing page returned 403. Portrait of a Graduate: I found no statewide portrait; the CASEL state page (a secondary source, which lists the same Guide) mentions none, and search turned up only district-level portraits (for example Christina). Not enough to call it none or district-led, so left unknown.

frameworks.name: Delaware Social and Emotional Learning (SEL) Competencies
frameworks.notes: From the "Delaware SEL Competencies Introductory Guide" dated July 28, 2020 (draft released Jan 28, 2020, reviewed with CASEL). Five competency areas, 15 benchmarks (codes 1A-5B are Delaware's own), each with performance indicators for K-2, 3-5, 6-8, 9-12 and adults. The Guide says Delaware "adopted" the five areas but calls them competencies, not standards, and says they leave local choice; it does not mention a State Board vote. THE FILE IS A MIRROR: the copy opened is hosted on constantcontact.com and linked from CASEL; DDOE's own page returned 403 to me. Reviewer: replace officialUrl with the DDOE link and confirm the text. Titles are short paraphrases.

items.title: Awareness of one's own emotions
items.summary: Show awareness of one's own emotions: name them, describe what causes them, and (in later bands) talk about how they are expressed.

items.title: Awareness of personal qualities and interests
items.summary: Show awareness of one's own qualities, likes and interests and how they shape choices.

items.title: Awareness of strengths and opportunities for growth
items.summary: Show awareness of one's strengths and of where one can grow, with reflection skills building across grade bands.

items.title: Personal responsibility and advocacy
items.summary: Show a sense of personal responsibility and advocacy: following expectations, owning choices and consequences, and speaking up for oneself and others.

items.title: Identify outside resources and supports
items.summary: Identify trusted adults, peers and community resources and supports, and when to use them.

items.title: Manage emotions and behaviors constructively
items.summary: Understand and use strategies for managing one's own emotions and behaviors constructively.

items.title: Set, monitor, adapt and evaluate goals
items.summary: Set, monitor, adapt and evaluate one's own goals to achieve success in school and life.

items.title: Awareness of others' emotions, perspectives and social cues
items.summary: Show awareness and consideration of other people's emotions, perspectives and social cues.

items.title: Civic responsibility in multiple settings
items.summary: Show civic responsibility in school, home and community settings.

items.title: Respect for human dignity, culture and differences
items.summary: Show awareness and respect for human dignity, including culture and differences.

items.title: Positive communication and social skills
items.summary: Use positive communication and social skills to interact effectively with others.

items.title: Prevent, manage and resolve conflicts
items.summary: Show the ability to prevent, manage and resolve interpersonal conflicts in constructive ways.

items.title: Use multiple factors in decisions
items.summary: Consider and use multiple factors in decision making, including ethical and safety factors, personal and community responsibilities, and short- and long-term goals.

items.title: Develop and model effective decision-making skills
items.summary: Develop, carry out and model effective decision-making skills for academic and social situations.

alignments.framework: Delaware Social and Emotional Learning (SEL) Competencies
alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Stay in Control of Your Spirit" (series: Conflict & Self-Government; the objective is the same in every grade version). FNE's stated objective: "This lesson helps learners recognize what is happening inside them, separate feelings from actions..." Students notice what they feel inside during conflict or pressure and separate it from what they do, which builds awareness of one's own emotions. Limit: Focused on strong emotions; it does not teach naming a wide range of emotions or what triggers them.

Players pick every feeling that fits the clues in a scene. Limit: The scenes are about other people, not the player's own emotions.
